findings.title: Pennsylvania Department of Health revokes Sharon Regional Medical Center license and directs cessation of patient admissions / orderly closure
findings.publisher: WKBN First News / Nexstar Media (syndicated on AOL)
findings.exact_supporting_passage: issued an order revoking SRMC’s license to operate, ordering them to stop seeing patients and begin an orderly closure.
findings.service_line: Hospital acute care; emergency department; inpatient and outpatient services
findings.access_consequences: The Pennsylvania Department of Health revoked Sharon Regional Medical Center's license and directed the facility to stop seeing patients and conduct an orderly closure. Sharon Regional had already halted emergency operations on November 4 and announced suspension of broader hospital services by November 6, so this finding is the newly corroborated regulatory action, not a second hospital closure. Patients must obtain emergency and other hospital services elsewhere; regional alternatives cited include UPMC facilities in Farrell, Greenville, and New Castle.
findings.affected_population: Patients served by Sharon Regional Medical Center and the surrounding Shenango Valley / Mercer County area; number affected not verified.
findings.evidence_notes: WKBN's original reporting, republished verbatim by AOL, quotes Gov. Josh Shapiro's office confirming a Pennsylvania Department of Health license-revocation order. The original WKBN webpage was robots-blocked, but the syndication was accessible. A secondary aggregation asserts a November 17 license effective date and a November 4 admissions ban, but the original written state order was not retrieved; effective_date intentionally null. Earlier supplementary heartbeats covered the hospital closure and flagged the license action as unverified; this run adds direct state-office confirmation via local reporting. Compare with production collector before promoting; do not duplicate the previously recorded closure.
